title: Unsupervised Brain Anomaly Detection as a Bayesian Inverse Problem with Diffusion Prior
abstract: arXiv:2609.24265v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) aims to localize abnormal regions in medical scans without pixel-level annotations. A typical strategy seeks to reconstruct a pseudo-healthy image that preserves subject-specific anatomy. Recently, diffusion models have been proposed to perform UAD. However, these methods rely on heuristic noise schedules or synthetic corruptions to balance subject-specificity and anomaly removal. In this work, we propose an alternative formulation of UAD as a Bayesian inverse problem under a diffusion prior. First, we introduce a latent spatial anomaly mask that models pixel-wise consistency between a test image and its latent corresponding pseudo-healthy image. Then, we propose an approximation of the unknown generation process that links healthy anatomy, anomalies, and the observed image, enabling a well-defined likelihood within the Bayesian framework. Building on recent advances in diffusion-based inverse problem

translated_title: 将无监督脑部异常检测作为具有扩散先验的贝叶斯逆问题
translated_abstract: 无监督异常检测（UAD）旨在无需像素级标注的情况下定位医学扫描中的异常区域。一种典型策略是重建保留受试者特异性解剖结构的伪健康图像。最近，扩散模型被提出用于执行UAD。然而，这些方法依赖于启发式噪声调度或合成损坏来平衡受试者特异性和异常去除。在这项工作中，我们提出了UAD的另一种表述方式，即将其作为扩散先验下的贝叶斯逆问题。首先，我们引入了一个潜在空间异常掩码，用于建模测试图像与其潜在对应的伪健康图像之间的像素级一致性。然后，我们提出了对未知生成过程的近似，该过程将健康解剖结构、异常和观测图像联系起来，从而在贝叶斯框架内实现了明确定义的似然函数。基于扩散逆问题的最新进展……
tldr: 该论文将无监督脑部异常检测重新表述为具有扩散先验的贝叶斯逆问题，通过引入潜在空间异常掩码和对未知生成过程的近似，在无需像素级标注的情况下实现了异常定位。
en_tdlr: This paper reformulates unsupervised brain anomaly detection as a Bayesian inverse problem with a diffusion prior, introducing a latent spatial anomaly mask and an approximation of the unknown generation process to enable anomaly localization without pixel-level annotations.
